audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagrees between layers on five of seven rows: phases[0..2].side=Skill vs win=Anivia, phases[5].side=Skill vs win=Anivia, phases[6].side=Vladimir vs win=Anivia.
audit.why: Packet levelChart reads Anivia, Anivia, Anivia, Skill, Anivia, Anivia, Anivia — the content layer already matches it; the full layer does not. phases[6].why literally describes Anivia dominating while the side says Vladimir.
audit.corrected: phases[0],[1],[2],[5],[6].side set to Anivia; phases[3] stays Skill, phases[4] stays Anivia.

audit.why: Anivia spikes at Lost Chapter, level 6 and Rylai's/Seraph's. Vladimir's spike is level 9 into two items with Crimson Pact converting health to AP; Hemoplague is a flat 120s all game so his fight windows are rare.
audit.corrected: Recorded the 120s Hemoplague cooldown in breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interactions were never stated: Sanguine Pool's 2s untargetability eats a committed Flash Frost, Tides of Blood is blocked by minions, Transfusion and Tides cost him no mana, and Hemoplague amplifies damage you take before it detonates. wants.you[2] told you to group into Hemoplague windows 'to outheal his sustain', which is backwards.
audit.why: Riot text: Pool is 2s untargetable on 28/25/22/19/16; E 'can be blocked by enemy units'; Q and W and E all cost 0 mana; R makes 'affected enemies take increased damage'.
audit.corrected: Bait Pool with the 4s Frostbite before spending the stun; last-hit behind minions to eat his E; buy Grievous Wounds rather than trading into Hemoplague.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was mentioned only in the itemization report line and contradicted by wants.you[2].
audit.why: _missing flags needs-antiheal for this matchup: Transfusion and Hemoplague both heal him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flagged 'Use Sanguine Pool' in wants.foe[1] as a probable wrong name.
audit.why: False positive — Sanguine Pool is the real W name; the flag matched on the leading verb.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by pooling your commit, healing chip off with free Transfusions, then scaling past you.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. It governs your forward steps. - W Crystallize spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1 but only 16s at rank 5 — 2s untargetable eats a committed combo, so bait it with Frostbite before you spend Flash Frost. - Tides of Blood is blocked by minions and costs him health. - Hemoplague is 120s all game.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by making him spend Sanguine Pool early — once the 2s is gone he is a slow, mana-free mage stuck inside your Glacial Storm.

edits.before: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Frostbite is on a 4s cooldown — throw it first, and if he pools you have lost 50 mana instead of your stun.

edits.before: Vladimir whiffs Sanguine Pool and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Pool only covers 350 units — wall past it and he surfaces in your storm.

edits.before: That is Vladimir’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Transfusion is free and heals it back — poke with no stun threat just feeds him.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Vladimir walks straight at you.
edits.after: Hemoplague amplifies the damage you take before it detonates — caught out with no egg, that window kills you.

edits.before: Group your damage into Hemoplague windows to outheal his sustain
edits.after: Buy Grievous Wounds early — Transfusion and Hemoplague both heal him

notes: phases[6].why described Anivia owning teamfights while phases[6].side read Vladimir — the full layer was simply out of sync with win[] and the packet on five rows. wants.you[2] was factually inverted (Hemoplague amplifies damage taken by YOU, it is not a heal window for your team) and is replaced with the anti-heal instruction _missing asks for. Left mid/late/early and the whys alone — they are already grounded in Pool, Transfusion and Hemoplague specifically.
